definitions.explanation: Metal restraints placed around a person's wrists, typically used by police during an arrest.

examples.japanese: {犯人|はんにん}に{手錠|てじょう}をかけた。
{警察官|けいさつかん}は{容疑者|ようぎしゃ}に{手錠|てじょう}をかけて{連行|れんこう}した。
examples.english: The police officer handcuffed the suspect and took them away.

examples.japanese: {手錠|てじょう}をかけられたまま{裁判所|さいばんしょ}に{連|つ}れて{行|い}かれた。
examples.english: He was taken to the courthouse still in handcuffs.

notes: Composed of {手|て} (hand) + {錠|じょう} (lock). The standard collocation is {手錠|てじょう}をかける (to put handcuffs on someone). The passive form {手錠|てじょう}をかけられる (to be handcuffed) is also very common. In Japanese criminal procedure, handcuffing someone is a significant legal act. Frequently encountered in crime dramas, news reports, and detective fiction.
